classification.difficultyReason: Tally the five integer visit values and stack one dot per observation on a labelled number line; this directly applies the taught dot-plot method.

content.prompt:
A group of 30 people in the building trade were asked how many times in the last week they had visited a particular hardware shop. Their responses were:

$0\quad2\quad2\quad1\quad0\quad0\quad3\quad4\quad1\quad1\quad0\quad0\quad0\quad3\quad1$

$1\quad1\quad2\quad3\quad0\quad0\quad1\quad1\quad2\quad2\quad1\quad3\quad0\quad0\quad0$

Draw a dot plot for the data.

answer.short: Dots above 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 visits: 11, 9, 5, 4 and 1 respectively.
answer.worked: Count the occurrences of each number of visits: 0 occurs 11 times, 1 occurs 9 times, 2 occurs 5 times, 3 occurs 4 times and 4 occurs once. The frequencies total 30. Draw a number line labelled ‘Number of visits’ and stack one dot for each person above the corresponding value.

spec.description: Dot plot with one dot per observation and equal vertical spacing.
